items.title: Is Nvidia reloading Jensen Huang? 🔄
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks! ☀️

A historic summit is taking shape in Shenzhen, China, where US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

This will be the first three-way meeting between the leaders. Nuclear arms control and the conflict involving Iran are expected to lead the discussion, while Ukraine remains an important concern in the background.

Back to the markets 📈,

Dalal Street ended Monday on a mixed note with Nifty and Sensex up 0.6% each.

Banking stocks led the rally, with HDFC Bank and SBI among the top gainers. However, the broader market missed the party. The midcap index fell 313 points, with more stocks declining than advancing.

💡 Spotlight: Fuel costs fire up wholesale inflation 🔥

India’s wholesale inflation rose to 12.29% in October, up from 11.39% in September.

Note: It has now remained above 9% for four consecutive months.

Fuel and power drove most of the increase, with inflation in this category jumping to 32.84% from 25.85%. Prices of crude oil, electricity, metals and chemicals also increased, while food inflation eased slightly to 8.58%.

Wholesale inflation measures how quickly prices are rising for businesses before products reach consumers. If these higher fuel and material costs continue, companies may eventually pass some of them on through higher retail prices.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: investors did not like Warburg’s Pricol deal 😬

Pricol plunged nearly 20% after investors reacted negatively to Warburg Pincus’ plan to take control of the company’s largest business.

What is Pricol selling: the company had announced in June that it would separate its Driver Information and Connected Vehicle Solutions business, or DICVS, into a new company called Pricol Autotech.

However, that announcement covered only the plan to separate DICVS into Pricol Autotech. The market did not yet know who would buy it, at what price or who would control it.

This business makes digital dashboards and instrument clusters, vehicle sensors and telematics systems, connected-vehicle technology, digital cockpit systems. Its customers include vehicle manufacturers such as TVS Motor, Royal Enfield, Honda Motorcycle and Ather Energy.

Warburg Pincus, through its affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments, will buy the promoters’ entire 38.51% holding for up to ₹1,663 crore.

The concerns: first concern appears to be valuation.

Paying ₹1,663 crore for 38.51% values the entire Pricol Autotech business at roughly ₹4,300 crore. Some investors believe this is too low for a fast-growing automotive-electronics business generating 60% of Pricol’s revenue.

The second concern is where the money goes.

This is a sale of shares owned by Pricol’s promoters. Therefore, the ₹1,663 crore will go to the promoter-group sellers, not to Pricol Limited for expansion or debt reduction.

The third concern is uncertainty. Investors who bought Pricol as one combined business must now value two different listed companies under two different controlling shareholders.

Share

2. Supreme Court says no to Vedanta’s Videocon deal ⚖️

Vedanta fell nearly 3% after the Supreme Court refused to restore its group company’s controversial plan to acquire 13 Videocon companies.

Quick background: Videocon Group collapsed under a massive debt burden and entered India’s insolvency process. Twin Star Technologies, a Vedanta Group company, offered to take control of 13 Videocon businesses for ₹2,962 crore.

However, Videocon’s lenders and other creditors had admitted claims of around ₹65,000 crore.

Financial creditors were expected to recover less than 5% of their admitted claims. Some operational creditors, including businesses that supplied goods and services to Videocon, would receive only around 0.72%.

In simple words, lenders would wait years and still recover only a tiny portion of their money.

What happened then: lenders holding more than 95% of the voting rights originally approved Twin Star’s plan in 2020.

The National Company Law Tribunal, or NCLT, approved it in June 2021.

However, Bank of Maharashtra, IFCI and SIDBI challenged the decision. They said lenders would recover far too little and those opposing the deal should not be forced to wait years for repayment instead of receiving cash.

In January 2022, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal set aside the approval and sent the proposal back to the lenders.

Twin Star approached the Supreme Court and challenged the NCLAT’s decision which got rejected now.

The stock fell especially because a planned acquisition has become more uncertain and potentially more expensive.

Share

3. Jensen Huang reloading? 🔄

Jensen Huang is reportedly discussing a possible return to Nvidia, just days after resigning amid an extramarital affair controversy.

What’s going on: an online campaign called Stand with Jensen has collected more than 1.6 lakh signatures, asking Nvidia’s board to reinstate him while an independent investigation continues.

The petition lists Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan among its supporters.

Around 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, representing nearly 18% of its workforce.

The investor push: Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker have asked Nvidia’s board to take its time while selecting a permanent CEO.

They want the company to keep every option open, including Huang’s return.

Their argument: Huang spent 33 years building Nvidia into the company at the centre of the AI boom. Replacing that experience and his relationships with customers, suppliers and governments will not be easy.

Interestingly, as per the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a possible comeback with people close to him.

Some Silicon Valley allies are reportedly organising a “war room” to persuade Nvidia’s board and seek support from the White House.

But, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to choose an external CEO and undertake a “dramatic shake-up”.

Share

4. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🛞 TVS Srichakra and Belrise Industries jumped up to 9% after reporting healthy Q2 earnings data.

🏦 Yes Bank gained more than 3% after the RBI and other parties filed a review petition against the Supreme Court’s order on AT-1 bonds.

What went down ⬇️

📉 Kaynes Technology India hit a 20% lower circuit while Vikram Solar, Amber Enterprises and Tata Motors PV fell up to 8% after reporting Q2 results.

🚚 Mahindra Logistics slipped 13% after the company announced that MD & CEO Hemant Sikka would step down next month and named Mohammed Turra as his successor.

💨 Inox Wind tanked 8% as Q2 margins disappointed and CEO resigned.

🚰 VA Tech Wabag ended more than 7% lower after the Saudi Arabia Water Authority cancelled a ₹2,332 crore desalination plant project.

💊 Laurus Labs promoters sold shares worth ₹500 crore, stock down 8%.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

🌍 Trade talks: India and Egypt are exploring a free trade agreement (FTA) to reach $12 billion in bilateral trade, after trade surged 65% to $5.04 billion in the first half of FY27.

🤖 AI pact: India joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative, signing the San Francisco Declaration to secure AI supply chains and critical technologies amid growing competition with China.

🔌 Power partnership: Redington partnered with Spanish firm Salicru to distribute power backup and protection solutions across the Middle East and Africa, targeting data centres and businesses.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the weekday blues get to you.

items.title: AI sell-off sends foreign investors to India 💸
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks and Happy Mondayyyy! ☀️

The week ahead is packed with enough data and events to keep investors busy.

Back home, India’s October wholesale inflation and trade data will arrive on Monday. Crude oil prices, developments in West Asia, foreign investor activity and the rupee will also influence Dalal Street.

Globally, Nvidia’s Q3 results on Tuesday will be closely watched especially its outlook after the sudden leadership change. On Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve’s meeting minutes could indicate whether interest rates may remain high or rise again.

Then comes Thursday’s big AI test as Anthropic is expected to list on Nasdaq. Its debut will show whether investors are still willing to pay premium prices for fast-growing but heavily loss-making AI companies.

💡 Spotlight: Guess who is back 👀

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)!!! Yes, FPIs invested ₹84,290 crore in Indian equities during the first 13 days of November, reversing two consecutive months of heavy selling.

The shift comes as investors reduce their exposure to technology-heavy global markets following the sell-off in AI stocks. Indian large-cap companies are also beginning to look more attractive.

The buying has supported Indian markets, but experts remain cautious. It is still unclear whether foreign investors are returning for the long term or simply moving money temporarily.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: Novelis lets China units go for $265 million 👋

Novelis, the US-based aluminium company owned by India’s Hindalco, has agreed to sell two of its Chinese subsidiaries for approximately $265 million.

The deets: subsidiaries including Novelis (China) Aluminum Products and Novelis (Shanghai) Aluminum Trading to Shenzhen Hongzhi Industrial Investment or its affiliates.

The deal includes a possible additional payment of $10 million if certain conditions are met.

Note: Novelis is not completely leaving China. Its Zhenjiang operation, which serves aerospace and industrial customers, is held through a different subsidiary and is not included in this sale.

The two subsidiaries generated $376 million, or approximately ₹3,319 crore, in net sales during FY26. That sounds substantial, but it represented only around 1% of Hindalco’s total sales.

The why: the official filing did not explain the reason for the sale.

However, media reports link it to intensifying competition from Chinese manufacturers and a wider reassessment of China operations by global companies as supply chains shift.

Importantly, the sale also comes at a time when Novelis CFO Devinder Ahuja recently announced his resignation to pursue another opportunity.

Share

2. Suspension scare forces SpiceJet to report results ⚠️

Nothing speeds up overdue paperwork quite like the threat of a trading suspension.

SpiceJet has promised to publish its pending financial results by December 7 after BSE warned that trading in its shares could be discontinued.

What BSE said: SpiceJet has not submitted its financial results for two consecutive quarters including March and June 2026.

Therefore the company’s trading in the airline’s shares will be suspended from December 10 unless it clears all pending requirements by December 7.

As per Indian law, listed companies usually need to publish quarterly results within 45 days. Audited annual results must generally be filed within 60 days of the financial year ending.

What is happening at SpiceJet: the delayed results come while the airline is facing a much wider cash crunch.

Its domestic market share fell to just 0.6% in September, compared with nearly 15% in 2019. SpiceJet carried approximately 73,000 domestic passengers during the month, down from nearly 5.92 lakh in January.

Only nine of its 12 aircraft were operational in November. The remaining planes were grounded amid payment disputes with aircraft owners.

The airline is also struggling to pay smaller suppliers. It owed micro, small and medium enterprises ₹122.93 crore during April–September 2026. Of this, ₹63.03 crore remained unpaid beyond the legally permitted 45 days.

Why things became worse: SpiceJet was already dealing with grounded aircraft, delayed salaries and unpaid supplier bills.

The Middle East conflict added another problem. Higher crude prices increased aviation fuel costs, while airspace restrictions made some international routes longer and more expensive.

Share

3. A2B served a ₹1,600 crore deal 🍽️

Adyar Ananda Bhavan, better known as A2B, has sold a majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems for $180 million, or more than ₹1,600 crore.

It is one of the largest transactions in India’s food-service industry.

Quick context: A2B is a Chennai-based vegetarian restaurant, sweets and packaged-food company. Today, it has around 160 outlets in India and more than 30 overseas, including locations in the US, UK, Singapore, Malaysia and Australia.

Breaking it down: Bodhi Tree will now own more than half of A2B and gain control over major business decisions. Importantly, A2B’s founders have said the partnership will help make the company ready for public markets.

The exact stake purchased has not been disclosed. An industry estimate values the entire company at around $350 million, or roughly ₹3,100 crore.

A2B’s founding family has not sold the whole business. It will remain a shareholder and continue participating in the company’s growth.

The company’s revenue reached around ₹1,502 crore in FY25. A2B’s website now claims annual turnover exceeding ₹1,700 crore.

Bodhi Tree Systems is an investment and business-building platform created by American-British businessman James Murdoch and Uday Shankar, a top executive of the Reliance-Disney India joint venture

The why: the goal is to turn a trusted regional food brand into a professionally managed business with a bigger presence across India and overseas.

Share

4. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🏦 MSTC jumped 20% on the BSE after the company reported its strongest Q2 since listing and received in-principle approval from the RBI to operate a Trade Receivables Discounting System.

❄️ Amber Enterprises surged 10% after Q2 revenue grew significantly exceeding expectations, driven by strong performance in its electronics division.

✈️ SpiceJet is considering raising fresh funds by issuing new shares to investors, stock up 5%.

🛡️ PB Fintech gained 5% amid reports that IRDAI may issue another draft paper on distribution.

⚡ TD Power gained over 3% after management raised revenue guidance.

What went down ⬇️

🔻 Ola Electric, Voda Idea, Ruchira Papers, Venky’s, Grasim and KPI Green fell up to 4% after reporting Q2 earnings.

🛢️ Rising crude prices weighed on paint, airline and oil marketing stocks, with IndiGo falling 1% and HPCL losing 2%.

📉 Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance declined 3% each as gold prices slipped.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

📦 Trade deficit: India’s goods trade gap widened from $30.21 billion in September to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October. However, on a year-on-year basis, it narrowed from $42.58 billion in October 2025.

💳 Wallet approval: Paytm Payments Services received in-principle RBI approval to operate digital wallets and prepaid payment instruments, subject to completing a system and cybersecurity audit within six months.

📈 IPO plans: Carlsberg India may launch a $600 million IPO as early as January 2027, with its Danish parent looking to sell a 15% stake at a $4 billion valuation.

🚀 India bet: American pet-care and snacking giant Mars wants India among its five fastest-growing markets and is targeting over $1.2 billion in revenue by 2030.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the Monday blues get to you.

items.title: Jensen Huang logged out of Nvidia 🚨
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks and Happy Fridayyyyy! ☀️

This is bigger than the “Big Thing” we usually cover, so we are putting it right at the top.

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member on Thursday, ending his 33-year run at the company he helped build into the centre of the AI boom.

The stock fell nearly 9% in extended trading as investors reacted to the sudden leadership change.

The resignation came shortly after reports that Nvidia’s board was considering removing Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent successor. Huang will not retain a seat on Nvidia’s board.

Quick revision: Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife after reports connected him with Alice Huang, a business executive whom US intelligence reportedly suspected of working with Chinese intelligence. China has denied the allegation.

The New York Times later reported a separate relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who reported to Huang.

A small Indian angle: Indian-origin executive Aarti Shah, a former Eli Lilly digital chief and Nvidia director since 2020, was among the board members deciding Huang’s future.

The larger picture: the US and China are competing to lead the development of advanced AI technology. Nvidia’s chips are central to that race because they provide the computing power needed to build and run AI systems.

Meanwhile, back home 📈,

Dalal Street gained for a third consecutive session, with both the Nifty and Sensex closing higher.

Sector performance was mixed. Realty stocks led the gains, while banking and financial stocks remained firm.

Auto and FMCG stocks faced selling pressure, and IT stocks fell for a fourth straight session.

💡 Spotlight: MSCI shuffles its India lineup 🔀

MSCI has added LIC, Adani Green Energy, Coforge and Meesho to its India Standard Index and removed PI Industries. The changes take effect after markets close on November 30.

MSCI creates stock market indices that investors use to track markets and build portfolios.

It regularly reviews companies’ size, trading activity and shares available to investors, updating its indices to reflect market changes.

According to CNBC-TV18, India’s share of MSCI’s emerging markets index is expected to rise from around 12.9% to 13.15%.

The small-cap shuffle: India Small Cap Index will add E2E Networks, Apollo Micro Systems, HUDCO, AXISCADES Technologies, Shadowfax Technologies and PI Industries. Coforge will leave that index as it moves into the Standard Index.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: India’s retail inflation hits a two-year high 🛒

India’s retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, crossing the RBI’s upper limit of 6% for the first time in two years.

What drove the rise: food prices were the biggest factor. Food inflation climbed to 8.94% from 7.74% in September, with essentials such as onions, garlic and ginger becoming more expensive.

Food accounts for nearly 40% of the basket used to measure retail inflation, so rising grocery bills can significantly push up the overall figure.

Food prices rose faster in rural areas, where inflation reached 9.09%, compared with 8.68% in urban areas, according to provisional October data.

Beyond the kitchen:

  • Restaurants and accommodation: inflation increased to 10.06% from 9.36%.

  • Clothing and footwear: 4.96%, up from 3.93%.

  • Housing: 2.90%, up from 2.74%.

  • Healthcare: 2.05%, up from 1.40%.

  • Information and communication: 3.16%, up from 2.44%.

Inflation in personal care and other miscellaneous goods and services slowed to 10.14% from 13.75%. That means prices were still rising, but at a slower pace.

What happens next: the RBI targets inflation of 4%, with an acceptable range of 2-6%. October’s reading is above that range, but one month alone does not count as a formal failure. That happens when average inflation stays outside the range for three consecutive quarters.

The RBI will watch whether this rise fades or spreads to more goods and services.

Could food get costlier: weak rainfall and a possible El Niño weather pattern could hurt harvests and tighten supplies, keeping some food prices high.

Share

2. Not a good day for defence stocks 📉

Hindustan Aeronautics fell more than 2% as the company’s operating profitability fell short of market expectations.

By the numbers:

  • Net profit: up 16% YoY at ₹1,936 crore

  • Revenue: up 14.9% YoY at ₹7,613 crore

  • EBITDA: up 11.6% YoY at ₹1,739 crore

  • Margin: down to 22.8% from 23.5%

Why the fall: HAL’s revenue and net profit grew at a healthy pace. However, operating profit increased more slowly than revenue and missed analysts’ expectations.

In simple words, HAL sold more during the quarter but kept a slightly smaller operating profit from every ₹100 it earned.

The margin specifically fell as expenses increased faster than revenue.

The helicopter move: HAL has acquired the remaining 50% of HATSOFF Helicopter Training from CAE Canada.

HATSOFF provides simulator-based training for military and civilian helicopter pilots. It will now become HAL’s wholly owned subsidiary, giving the company complete control over the business and its future expansion.

While we are on earnings 📊,

Bharat Dynamics sold significantly more missiles and defence equipment in Q2, but earned less operating profit from those sales.

Its shares fell over 3% after the results as a sharp decline in margins overshadowed better-than-expected revenue growth.

By the numbers 📊:

  • Net profit: at ₹183 crore, down 15.3% YoY

  • Revenue: at ₹1,664 crore, up 45.1% YoY

  • EBITDA: at ₹101 crore, down 46.1% YoY

  • Margin: at 6.1%, down from 16.3% YoY

What happened: revenue was a clear positive.

The company delivered more orders, but those sales generated much lower operating margins.

Zoom out: demand is not the immediate concern for Bharat Dynamics. It has a large order book and the government continues to increase domestic defence procurement.

The bigger question is execution. The company must secure critical components on time, deliver orders faster and restore margins.

Share

3. How SoftBank lost $3.7B on AI equipment 🫣

SoftBank just lost $3.73 billion after overcommitting to power equipment for its planned AI data centres.

Masayoshi Son’s company reserved gas turbines years in advance, even before its projects’ requirements were finalised. When those plans changed, billions in advance payments were lost.

And with turbine manufacturers already booking delivery slots for 2032, SoftBank’s mistake exposes an expensive problem facing the AI infrastructure boom.

Read more

4. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🏡 Godrej Industries rallied 11% after Temasek invested ₹2,500 crore in Godrej Capital, valuing it at up to ₹28,000 crore.

⚡️Bajaj Finance rose over 3% following the launch of its qualified institutional placement to raise funds from institutional investors.

✨ Kalyan Jewellers gained 7% and over 20% during the week after Q2 FY27 consolidated profit rose 64% YoY to ₹427 crore.

😮‍💨 HDFC Life gained nearly 4%, its highest since June, as October premium income rose 17.8% to ₹3,334 crore.

🚀 SBI Life gained nearly 3% as October first-year premium income rose 11.6% YoY to ₹3,556 crore.

What went down ⬇️

👎🏻 Page Industries fell over 12% after subdued Q2 results, despite revenue rising 11.5% YoY to ₹1,439.6 crore from ₹1,291 crore.

📉 Caplin Point Laboratories slipped over 5% despite September-quarter revenue rising 18% YoY and profit increasing 15.3% to ₹178 crore.

❌ Chennai Petroleum, ONGC, Oil India and other oil stocks fell 1-3% as global crude prices declined.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

🏗️ Mega investment: ReNew plans to invest ₹80,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh across green data centres, solar manufacturing and permanent magnet production.

🏢 Leadership change: Tata Steel CEO TV Narendran will take over as Tata International chairman, succeeding Noel Tata amid leadership changes across the Tata Group.

📈 IPO plans: Haldiram Snacks has reportedly begun preparations for a potential ₹10,000 crore IPO, targeting a listing in late 2027.

And that’s a wrap. Pour yourself an extra one this weekend 🥂

We’ll be back like clockwork on Monday!

items.title: Losses loom for OpenAI 🫤
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks! ☀️

A solid Wednesday for Indian markets, with the Sensex and Nifty closing at fresh nine-month highs, supported by buying in financial stocks and gains across several sectors.

Auto, banking and FMCG stocks led the rally, while pharma and healthcare remained relatively subdued.

💡 Spotlight: falling crude prices lift these stocks 💪🏻

Shares of IndiGo, Asian Paints, Apollo Tyres and several oil marketing companies rose 2-4% after Brent crude fell nearly 3% to $89.66 a barrel on Tuesday morning, its lowest level since August 31.

Oil prices dropped after US president Donald Trump said the war on Iran is ‘effectively over.’

What drove the rally: cheaper crude could lower costs for airlines, paint makers and tyre manufacturers, boosting investor sentiment. The stocks gained even as oil prices recovered modestly amid renewed concerns over shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Why these sectors benefit: they rely heavily on petroleum-based fuels and raw materials.

For IndiGo, aviation turbine fuel is a major expense. A sustained fall in crude prices could lower fuel bills and improve profitability.

Paint makers, including Asian Paints, Berger Paints and Kansai Nerolac, could benefit from cheaper petroleum-based raw materials and solvents.

Tyre manufacturers, such as Apollo Tyres, CEAT and JK Tyre, could also see lower costs for inputs such as synthetic rubber and carbon black.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: A fertiliser cushion for farmers 🧑‍🌾

The Union Cabinet approved a ₹62,370 crore fertiliser subsidy package for the Rabi 2026-27 season, up 64% from ₹37,952 crore last year. The package will help keep Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP), a widely used fertiliser, available to farmers at ₹1,350 per bag.

How it works: the government pays part of the cost of these fertilisers to companies that make or import them, helping farmers buy them at lower prices.

It decides how much to pay each crop season, based on fertiliser prices in India and abroad, along with the cost of making them.

The government also approved ₹41,534 crore for the Kharif 2026 season. These fertilisers help farmers grow wheat, pulses and oilseeds.

Why it matters: India’s fertiliser imports rose 36% between FY24 and FY26, leaving it exposed to global price swings. The subsidy helps cushion farmers from higher costs as they prepare to sow winter crops.

Market reaction: fertiliser stocks rose as the package is expected to help companies supply affordable fertilisers despite higher production costs.

Shares of Fertilisers and Chemicals Travancore (FACT), Coromandel International and Gujarat State Fertilisers and Chemicals (GSFC) gained between 3-8%.

Share

2. OpenAI’s $10B quarter still ends in losses 🤯

OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reached $10 billion for the first time, but the company still lost more money than it earned.

What happened: revenue increased nearly 50% from the previous quarter and almost tripled from last year.

Note: the numbers were reportedly shared with investors during a call on Tuesday. OpenAI has not publicly released the results or commented on the reports.

By the numbers 📊:

  • Operating loss at $10.9 billion, up from $10.1 billion.

  • Operating margin at (-)109%, compared with (-)150% in Q2

  • Annualised revenue at roughly $50 billion at the end of September

A -109% operating margin means OpenAI lost around $109 from its regular business operations for every $100 it earned.

OpenAI is also entering travel: alongside the financial update, OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a young AI travel startup founded by Francis Davidson.

Odessia allowed users to plan and organise trips through an AI travel agent. It had raised $6 million in early funding led by Sequoia and launched its product only around five months ago.

The purchase price has not been disclosed.

3. ’Tis the season for losses? 🤔

Air India’s net loss exceeded ₹10,000 crore in the first half of FY27, according to disclosures by Singapore Airlines (SIA), which owns a 25.1% stake in the carrier. That’s nearly half its ₹22,000 crore loss for the whole of FY26.

Breaking it down: SIA reports its share of Air India’s losses in its own results. This fell about 15.8% from 429.5 million Singapore dollars a year earlier, suggesting that Air India’s losses narrowed.

Using the same exchange rate, Air India’s estimated loss in the first half of FY26 would have been around ₹12,900 crore.

The improvement offered some relief to SIA, but Air India continues to weigh on its earnings.

The impact on SIA: Singapore Airlines’ net profit fell 43.9% YoY to 134 million Singapore dollars in the first half of FY27.

Lower losses at companies it partly owns, mainly Air India, boosted earnings by 68 million Singapore dollars. A lower tax bill provided another 70 million Singapore dollars boost.

Background: SIA’s partnership with Tata Sons began in 2013, when they set up Vistara. After Vistara merged with Air India in November 2024, SIA received a 25.1% stake in the combined airline and invested another 360 million Singapore dollars.

Share

4. Why do India’s electricity prices swing so wildly? 👀

Green electricity prices on the Indian Energy Exchange jumped 67% in October 2026, reaching ₹4.13 per unit. Yet, during some trading intervals that same month, wholesale electricity prices fell close to zero.

The problem? India is generating plenty of solar power during the day, sometimes more than the grid can absorb.

But after sunset, solar generation drops while electricity demand continues, pushing prices higher.

Read More

5. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🔥 Jyoti Structures surged 19% after securing access to bank credit worth over ₹500 crore to execute its existing order book.

🚀 IIFL Finance gained 6% following the Blackstone deal and its board’s approval for a capital raise of ₹6,414 crore.

📈 Kalyan Jewellers went up over 8% after Q2 profit rose 64% YoY. UBS retained ‘Buy’ with a ₹900 price target.

💪🏻 Ashoka Buildcon rallied over 10% after securing an NHAI road project worth ₹865.9 crore.

😮‍💨 IRFC rose 3%, marking the biggest single-day gain since December 2025 as railway stocks rallied.

👆BHEL gained 2% after securing a ₹600-900 crore Power Grid order for two synchronous condensers in Gujarat’s Kalyanpur.

What went down ⬇️

📉 Cochin Shipyard tumbled nearly 7% after consolidated net profit fell 50% to ₹53.77 crore in the September quarter, from ₹107.5 crore a year earlier.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

📈 Growth upgrade: Moody’s raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7%, citing strong consumption, improving investments and solid economic fundamentals.

📉 MF slowdown: Equity mutual fund inflows fell 13.8% to ₹32,994 crore in October, with sharper declines in small-cap and mid-cap funds, while total AUM rose to ₹83.39 lakh crore.

💸 Tax collections: Net direct tax collections rose 11.76% to ₹14.42 lakh crore through November 10, while gross collections grew 14.02% in FY27.

💻 India layoffs: Qualcomm has begun layoffs in India, with over 1,000 employees potentially affected, including long-serving staff with strong performance records.

🤝 Leadership appointment: Sarvam appointed former Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as its President and Chief Business Officer (CBO).

📈 Market shakeup: Microsoft overtook Nvidia as the world’s second-most valuable company, as Nvidia shares fell over 6% amid reports of a probe involving CEO Jensen Huang.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the weekday blues get to you.

items.title: Jensen Huang weighs a comeback at Nvidia
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 9,924 new readers. The last time a board’s call sparked this kind of backlash? OpenAI’s firing of Sam Altman in 2023. Three years later, a swell of Nvidia employees and tech titans is hoping for a similar outcome for Jensen Huang.

A petition demanding his return just topped 140K signatures in a matter of days, Elon Musk’s among them, and big investors want the door left open. Now, the Financial Times also says the man at the heart of it all has been privately mulling a comeback.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Musk, Nvidia staff rally to bring back Jensen Huang

  • The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

  • Turn a messy plan into a shared board

  • Report: OpenAI folds robotics team into core research

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

JENSEN HUANG & NVIDIA

🔄 Musk, Nvidia staff rally to bring back Jensen Huang

Image source: X / petition website / The Rundown

The Rundown: Elon Musk, Nvidia employees, and top investors are pushing Nvidia’s board to reconsider Jensen Huang’s exit, with an online petition to reinstate him passing 140K signatures days after the co-founder resigned amid multiple reported affairs.

The details:

  • The petition argues Huang was removed before any proof of spying surfaced or an outside probe even concluded, and calls for “due process, not mob justice.”

  • Over 7,000 signers claim to be Nvidia staff, and in an earlier poll on anonymous app Blind, 88% of 232 Nvidia staffers said Huang should stay.

  • Musk signed the petition, arguing Nvidia’s supply deals are exposed without Huang because “many… were a handshake with Jensen, not a contract.”

  • The board has yet to respond publicly and is still picking a search firm, while reports say Huang has been “participating in the process” of picking his successor.

  • A Financial Times report also revealed that Huang is privately weighing a return, with an ally building a “war room” of tech execs to help lobby for it.

Why it matters: Nvidia is nothing without its people? The Jensen saga is entering its OpenAI-Altman moment, when staff and investor pressure got Sam his job back days after his ouster. Altman’s drama stayed mostly internal, while Jensen’s has spilled into geopolitics, Congress, and the FBI — but his backers are eyeing a similar resolution.

TOGETHER WITH OPENART

💬 Create ads in your AI assistant with OpenArt MCP

The Rundown: OpenArt MCP brings OpenArt’s image and video ad tools into AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT. No prompt expertise needed: just describe what you want in simple language and share a product photo or link. Built-in skills ask for details, plan scripts and shots, and create a draft for you to review before a final version.

With OpenArt MCP, you can:

  • Turn a product photo or link into a product listing video or a TV-style commercial

  • Turn one script into a creator ad, a polished presenter video, or a talking head

  • Generate multiple ad variations at once with different hooks, headlines, or scenes

Add OpenArt MCP.

THE RUNDOWN ROUNDTABLE

💡 The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

The Rundown: The Rundown Roundtable is a weekly feature where we poll members of The Rundown staff about how we use AI in our work and daily lives.

Zach, Editor-in-Chief: As more of a creative type, I’ve never loved data analysis. Finding the right numbers used to take forever, and I wasn't even sure I was comparing the right things once I had them. Now I connect Claude to Beehiiv, our newsletter platform, and work through the numbers conversationally.

Each week I have a scheduled task to run our stats report. Claude pulls open rates, clicks, reader ratings, comments, and more for all three of our newsletters, surfacing themes and notes across issues. I also built a filter to weed out bot clicks and fake poll votes, and I package it all into a page I present in our team meeting.

The follow-up questions are where I really feel the value. With the data in front of me, I can keep poking at issues, ask for more, or troubleshoot on the fly in the same chat with the context already there.

The connector has helped me dig into the data and run tests without my eyes glazing over, and made me more comfortable actually diving into an important area that I used to dread.

Brooke, Community Engagement Lead: I run our support inbox solo, and the same questions kept coming up. I wanted my team to see what members were actually writing in about instead of it living in my head. I just finished building this with Claude connected to our Gmail support inbox, plus Slack and scheduled tasks.

Every Thursday, Claude reads the week's support threads and filters out spam and noise. It groups the real member questions by theme, then by the team that can fix them. It drafts one short post per team covering the top thing members ran into and a suggested fix. I review, tweak, and send each post to that team's Slack channel before our Friday meeting.

At the start of each month, Claude audits the full month of tickets: what drove volume, what changed from last month, and what's a product gap versus a one-off. It also checks my saved replies against what members actually asked. The goal is recurring tickets fixed at the source instead of answered over and over.

AI TRAINING

👨🏻‍🏫 Turn a messy plan into a shared board

The Rundown: Claude Whiteboards turns a messy plan you talk through or paste into a board your team can edit. In this guide, you'll build one, check what Claude laid out, fix it, and share it with your team.

Step-by-step:

  1. In Claude's sidebar, click Artifacts, then the Whiteboard tile under Make something new. A blank board opens

  2. Click Chat at the top of the board and talk your plan through with the microphone, or paste it in. Include owners and any dates you know

  3. Read Claude's reply and the board it builds. Claude fills gaps with its own guesses, so check every owner, date, and arrow against what you said

  4. Fix small things with the toolbar at the bottom. To rework one area, drag a box around it, click Chat in the toolbar, and describe the change

  5. Click Share, invite teammates by email, and choose Editor, Commenter, or Viewer. Invites start on Commenter

Pro tip: Before you invite anyone, settle the dates Claude guessed with their owners. On our test board, two later tasks hung off one guessed date.

Watch the full guide at The Rundown University →

PRESENTED BY COLLIBRA

👀 Your AI agents are working. Who’s watching?

The Rundown: Agents now read, decide, and act across your tools, and the fleet grows whether you govern it or not. Drift, not hackers, is the usual failure. Collibra’s playbook shows how to scan every agent, set fleet-wide rules, and catch problems early.

The playbook covers:

  • How to build governance for autonomy to scale agents

  • Where to start for your specific use case

  • A 10-step plan and maturity self-assessment

Get the playbook.

OPENAI

🤖 Report: OpenAI folds robotics team into core research

Image source: Robocurve

The Rundown: OpenAI moved its robotics team into its main research and product groups, according to Fortune, with the company saying GPT-6 Astra and other models can run robots without a separate brain — though staffers soon disputed the claim.

The details:

  • OpenAI says general models like GPT-6 Astra can be put to work on robots directly, instead of needing specialized or world models as previously thought.

  • The company previously shuttered its robotics division in 2020 and rebooted it in 2024, with Sam Altman saying OpenAI is pursuing a humanoid of its own.

  • Engineer David Schnurr called OpenAI robotics “alive and well” and pointed to 15 open roles, months after Sam Altman’s May hiring push for the team.

  • Others also pushed back, with one staffer calling the report “completely wrong” and another saying OpenAI robotics still had the “same program, roadmap, goals.”

Why it matters: This feels less like an “OpenAI isn’t prioritizing robotics” story and more like a “general models can do more than we anticipated” one. We’ve seen robotics breakthroughs across top labs. Now, with frontier models running things themselves, improving the robot’s brain may be a bigger research need than the hardware itself.

▸ Nav built an AI tutoring tracker to see if lessons actually work

Today's workflow comes from reader Nav:

“I'm a parent with two boys, one preparing for GCSEs and the other for the 11+ entrance exams, and they have several tutors covering Maths, English, Science and Music Theory. I wanted a better way to manage their education and to understand whether they were actually making progress. This is a parent-built system, not a commercial education product, and I developed it using AI tools without needing traditional software development skills.

I record tutoring sessions and use Otter.ai to generate transcripts. I use ChatGPT to review the Otter transcripts, summarize each lesson, identify areas of weakness, extract homework, and recommend follow-up actions. It also compares feedback across sessions to see whether particular learning gaps are improving.

On Fridays, I hold a progress checkpoint where ChatGPT helps review recent lessons, highlight learning gaps, identify overdue actions, and suggest what to prioritise with each tutor. The biggest benefit is that I'm no longer just paying for tutoring and hoping it's working.”

items.title: Nvidia enters life without Jensen Huang

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,207 new readers. Two weeks ago, a NYT report tied Nvidia’s CEO to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Now, the man who turned a Denny’s-booth startup into the engine of the AI boom is out the door.

Jensen Huang has resigned after a 33-year run at Nvidia, leaving the world’s most important AI infrastructure company without its founder, and without a clear plan for what comes next.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia’s CEO

  • Rowan’s Corner: How I use AI to coach my calls

  • Build a shared tracker in Claude Sheets

  • Google joins the race for your face with AI glasses

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🚨 Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia’s CEO

Image source: Nvidia / The Rundown

The Rundown: Jensen Huang just resigned as Nvidia’s CEO and board member, effective immediately, after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset; CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.

The details:

  • The exit came days after Huang admitted to infidelity following reports linking him to an alleged Chinese spy. The board backed him, saying it had “no reason to believe” national security or company secrets were compromised.

  • Pressure built after the NYT reported a second relationship with an Nvidia executive; Reuters reported a third with another employee after the resignation.

  • Kress, CFO since 2013, will hold both roles as the board looks for a replacement, with Trump pitching Tim Cook as the “only one man” who could take the job.

  • Nvidia closed down 4% Thursday after falling more than 14%, with earnings due Nov. 17 and House committee chairs seeking a closed-door briefing from Huang.

Why it matters: Over 33 years, Huang made Nvidia the company it is, taking it from gaming GPUs to the hardware behind modern AI. Under him, it stayed dominant even as rivals pushed their own chips. Whoever steps into his shoes will have to build on that and decide which of his fights to keep, from lighter AI regulation to chip sales to China.

TOGETHER WITH HUBSPOT

🧠 100+ ChatGPT prompts to revolutionize your workflow

The Rundown: HubSpot’s free, comprehensive “How to Use ChatGPT at Work” guide provides 100+ ready-to-use prompts to help professionals boost efficiency and adopt AI-driven workflows.

Inside, you’ll find:

  • Quick crash course to master ChatGPT in under 30 minutes

  • Practical industry use cases to spark real-world inspiration

  • 100+ prompts to streamline tasks and accelerate productivity

  • Expert tips to tackle common AI roadblocks with confidence

Get your free copy.

ROWAN’S CORNER

📞 How I use AI to coach my calls

Screenshot via Forbes interview with Rowan

Rowan: After every high-stakes call, I let AI tear apart my performance. It started as a weird quirk several months ago, and it’s quietly become one of my most useful habits, so I figured it’s worth sharing.

The setup is simple. I record my meetings with Granola (you could use any meeting note taker), connect the transcripts to Claude, and instead of just pulling summaries and action items, I make it look backward at my own performance.

A few of the analyses I run:

  • My talk ratio on sales calls, flagged whenever it passes 50% (typically you want to talk less)

  • Every moment I dodged a hard topic or put off a decision I could’ve made on the spot

  • A commitment log of everything promised, including every “let me think about it,” which gets pushed into my to-do lists

  • An objection library of every pushback partners raised this year, with a stronger answer drafted for each

One quick tip if you try this is to ask for exact quotes, so Claude or ChatGPT puts your own words next to what you should’ve said.

And this works for way more than my calls. You could run the same workflow on recruiting calls, sales calls, leadership meetings, heck, even podcasts and interview recordings. If it’s recorded, it can coach you.

AI TRAINING

💻️ Build a shared tracker in Claude Sheets

The Rundown: Claude now builds its own spreadsheets, turning a description into a table and leaving the formulas in the cells, so you can check every number. In this guide, you’ll build a campaign tracker with status and budget, then share it for editing.

Step-by-step:

  1. Go to claude.ai/artifacts, click the green Sheets tile under Make something new, and describe the tracker: every column, dropdown values, and cells with formulas

  2. Click a total and read the formula bar. Then select the table, click Ask Claude, and ask it to point out any cell holding a typed number instead of a formula, since only formulas update when Spent changes

  3. Ask Claude to highlight tasks that are past their due date and not Done. Then paste your own tasks over the samples and have Claude delete the leftovers

  4. Click Share, invite a teammate with Can edit, and leave General access on Only you. On paid plans, people can edit cells but can’t ask Claude for changes

Pro tip: Before any big change, open Share, then the Export tab, and download an Excel copy. If an edit goes wrong, you still have the tracker as it was. For a bad build, Undo on the “Claude updated” notice takes the whole thing back.

Watch the full guide at The Rundown University →

PRESENTED BY INCOGNI

📞 That scam call wasn’t random

The Rundown: Scammers don’t guess your number — they buy it from data brokers selling your phone, home address, and relatives’ info online. That’s how a random call turns into phishing, impersonation, or worse. Incogni removes your data from these databases and keeps removing it automatically.

With Incogni working in the background, you can:

  • Keep phone numbers and addresses off broker databases

  • Reduce exposure to identity theft and impersonation

  • Let automated removals do the work continuously

Get 58% off with the code RUNDOWN.

GOOGLE

👓️ Google joins the race for your face with AI glasses

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google opened pre-orders for its first Gemini-powered AI smart glasses, 18 months after announcing them at I/O 2025, with frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster starting at $395 in a direct challenge to Meta’s Ray-Bans.

The details:

  • Built with Samsung, the nine styles pack a 12MP camera, open-ear speakers, and up to nine hours of battery into 41-gram frames, with no display in the lenses.

  • Wearers can say “Hey Gemini” to ask about what they’re looking at, get Maps directions in their ear, play music, or translate speech live across 70+ languages.

  • Google says the glasses redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini sees them, show a light when recording, and stop recording if the light is covered; users can even control which apps access the camera and mic.

  • They go on sale Dec. 10 in the U.S. and South Korea and work with iPhones too, taking on Meta, which shipped 81% of AI glasses in the first half of the year.

Why it matters: Meta holds the crown in AI glasses, but privacy backlash over their cameras has dogged it, to the point it launched a camera-free model in September. With its new glasses and their added privacy features, Google is pitching itself as the safer pick, betting it can keep the camera and still earn the trust Meta has struggled to win.

▸ A Rundown reader used AI to turn personal stories into published books

Today’s workflow comes from an anonymous Rundown reader:

“After retiring from medicine, I began writing personal stories and used ChatGPT to polish them for sharing. Over time, it helped me connect stories, identify larger themes, and explore new ideas. I bring my own stories, reflections, and questions, then work with ChatGPT through suggestions, revisions, and sometimes disagreements. I also use Claude and Gemini as independent reviewers to catch weaknesses or missed possibilities, while keeping all creative and editorial decisions my own.

This process has helped me publish books and create Creating Space, a collection of contemplative resources for individuals and groups. Each project sparks new questions and ideas. The biggest benefit hasn’t been saving time. At 73, I’ve begun to see myself as a creator, using AI to explore possibilities and bring my ideas to life while retaining responsibility for the work.”

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,952 new readers. Jensen Huang has been Nvidia’s center of gravity since 1993, long enough to turn it into the engine of the entire AI boom. That run may suddenly be down to its final days.

A new report says directors are preparing to push the co-founder out as CEO, hours after a second affair surfaced, this one with an executive who reports to him. As crazy as it would’ve sounded a few weeks ago, Nvidia without Jensen is no longer unthinkable.

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🚪 Jensen Huang’s job in doubt after second affair report

Image source: Creative Commons / The Rundown

The Rundown: Nvidia’s directors are preparing to remove Jensen Huang as CEO, according to The Wall Street Journal, just hours after The New York Times reported a second affair for the co-founder — this time with a vice president who answers to him.

The details:

  • Five people who’ve worked at Nvidia told the NYT that Jensen and Kimberly Powell, its health care VP, had an affair that’s been discussed internally.

  • Jensen’s security reportedly offered an NDA after someone filmed the two being ‘affectionate’ during a March conference, though the NYT hasn’t seen the video.

  • The Economist called for Jensen to resign for his involvement with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, with members of Congress also pushing for his exit.

  • Nvidia lost over $427B in market value in two sessions after the affair came out, rose Wednesday, then fell about 8% after hours as the two reports landed.

Why it matters: Nvidia ranks among the world’s biggest companies; its chips train nearly every major AI, and almost all of that runs through Jensen. With roughly 60 direct reports and a rockstar persona that customers treat as the company’s face, there’s no playbook for replacing him — and a major shock to the system may be incoming.

TOGETHER WITH PLAID

🔌 Plaid powers Finances in ChatGPT

The Rundown: Plaid’s secure, permissioned data access gives ChatGPT the financial context it needs to give people personalized answers to their money questions. Hear from Ethan Bloch, OpenAI’s Product Lead, Personal Finance, on why secure connectivity and financial context are foundational to the experience.

NATE’S NOTEBOOK

🗂️ Claude Projects now take their own notes

The Rundown: Each week, Rundown AI educator Nate Grahek breaks down what he’s seeing while teaching real teams to use AI.

Nate: Claude Projects on the web can now save their own knowledge files. It went seemingly unnoticed, and I think it matters more than any demo you saw this week.

You know the demos: Fable 5.2 had 1,000 agents build an entire operating system in eight days. That’s good for clicks, but it doesn’t apply to getting real work done.

What gets real work done is context. For three years, I’ve taught that Claude needs to know the way you do the work, in your role, at your organization. Set up a Project once with the documents that show how you do a proposal the right way, and it reuses them over and over. On the web, that Project works on any of your devices, and you can share it with your team.

The catch was that Claude couldn’t add to it. If you wanted Claude to save its research and compare it against next week’s, you had to work locally, and that closed the door on your phone and easy sharing.

Now, Claude can do the research, synthesize the main ideas, and save them as new knowledge files in the Project. Put it on a schedule, and it’s gathering and curating its own knowledge, both inside and outside your organization.

Projects have long been Claude’s killer feature, and one tiny detail just made them even better.

P.S. — If you’re interested in learning about how to utilize Claude to its full potential, join me at today’s free workshop.

GOOGLE DEEPMIND

🔬 Google’s new AlphaGenome traces disease to cells

Image source: Google DeepMind

The Rundown: DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, an AI that predicts how small DNA differences between people play out inside specific cell types — a more detailed view than the original that could help trace diseases back to the cell types involved.

The details:

  • DeepMind’s Adam Gayoso called it “tying human genetics to cell biology,” as the original version averaged whole tissues while version 2 studies each cell type.

  • The original caught just 16% of the DNA changes behind gene shifts in a test on 28 immune cell types, with AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubling it to 30%.

  • Labs can also hand it gene activity from just a few dozen cells, like immune cells fired up by a vaccine, and get predictions without having to retrain the model.

  • Tested on inflammatory bowel disease, the model matched a recent study by picking out a DNA change that overworks one gene in the gut’s immune cells.

Why it matters: Scientists have found plenty of DNA quirks tied to diseases like type 2 diabetes, but they often can’t tell which cells they actually impact — the part drug makers need. AlphaGenome 2 helps answer that question and identify the experiments worth running first, which could mean better-aimed treatments for common illnesses.

items.title: OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,653 new readers. Google conditioned companies to obsess over their search listings for decades. That same scramble has been playing out on AI platforms, and OpenAI just gave brands an official way in.

Its new ‘Businesses’ beta gives brands a verified profile, a view of their mentions, and a personalized AI agent for direct buyer questions, opening a new way to meet customers where they’re increasingly searching… inside ChatGPT.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

  • Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

  • Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

  • ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

OPENAI

🛒 OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta hub where brands can claim a verified profile, track how often the chatbot mentions them, and set up AI agents for shoppers, which paid ads can now point to.

The details:

  • Profiles are currently free to claim for eligible companies, while agents are live first for U.S. online retailers and digital service firms.

  • Brands can write their agent’s instructions and add product details, with shoppers opening it from the profile in a labeled chat separate from ChatGPT’s answers.

  • A dashboard shows how often ChatGPT mentions a brand and drives clicks to its site, plus “discovery topics” that can point to gaps in what the brand shares.

  • OpenAI first piloted ad-linked agents in September, and brands can now pay to make their agent the landing spot for ads in ChatGPT, with each paid spot labeled.

Why it matters: Brands used to fight for a spot in Google’s results, and in the AI era, that’s shifted to getting name-dropped by the assistants themselves. Companies were mostly guessing what ChatGPT said about them or paying outside specialists to find out. OAI just handed them that visibility directly, plus a one-on-one line to potential customers right inside the chat.

TOGETHER WITH MEMOKET

🗓️ Your conversations, now in Apple Calendar

The Rundown: Memoket Gem is an AI wristband that captures conversations with one press and turns them into summaries, action items, and connected memory. Now with Apple Calendar integration: connect in the Memoket iPhone app to automatically sync new recordings as calendar events.

With Memoket, you can:

  • Find recordings by when the conversation happened

  • Revisit decisions and context across conversations

  • Bring relevant memories into ChatGPT and Claude

  • Use the app on your Apple Watch, coming this month

Discover Memoket Gem.

ANTHROPIC

🗄️ Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

Image source: Anthropic

The Rundown: Anthropic just rolled out Claude Sheets and Whiteboards in beta — spreadsheets and shared boards Claude builds alongside a team — while making its Claude Data analytics tool generally available and announcing Claude Meetings, an assistant that sits in on video calls.

The details:

  • Sheets can build a working spreadsheet with formulas via prompt and export it to Excel, while Whiteboards maps a plan onto a shared board for a team to edit.

  • Claude Data, originally named Dashboards when it entered beta in October, turns company metrics into narrated videos and visual data stories.

  • Product lead Nicholas Lin said Claude joins nearly every Anthropic meeting after months of testing, with a Google Meet beta coming to Team and Enterprise users.

  • Upgraded connectors, the links between Claude and other work apps, now also open tools like Adobe and Atlassian fully inside Claude without switching platforms.

Why it matters: Claude continues to eat both legacy office software and the newer apps that followed, with spreadsheets, dashboards, and meeting tools now joining Slides, Design, and Docs. The apps it hasn’t rebuilt now open inside Claude anyway, pulling more use into the AI assistant and away from the tools the workday used to run on.

AI TRAINING

🌐 Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use ChatGPT’s updated Chrome extension to compare open pages, check the facts, and group the tabs you need. Start in Chat to read, then use Work for a browser action you approve.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install the official ChatGPT extension from OpenAI and open its side panel. Use a practice Chrome profile with public pages for your first run

  2. Open three pricing pages and tell ChatGPT which tabs to read. Give it your team size, required features, budget, and billing period

  3. Check the comparison against the pages. Confirm the full team cost and leave missing details unverified rather than guessing

  4. Switch to Work where available and ask it to group only those three tabs. Review the list first, then check the actual group in Chrome

  5. Ask for a short recommendation with source links and one question to resolve. Keep trials, purchases, and messages outside the task

Pro tip: Use the same side panel on any article. Select the tab and ask ChatGPT for the main claim, the evidence, and what the author leaves unresolved.

PRESENTED BY GARTNER

🎰 Only 1 in 5 AI use cases pays off  

The Rundown: Enterprise AI use cases grew by 400% this year, but not all are delivering ROI. Investment without value only creates bad momentum. These Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo takeaways show what separates mere AI activity from real, measurable results.

What you’ll learn:

  • How to build momentum that compounds value

  • Ways to prevent key risks

  • How to make people your AI safety net

Download the insights.

AI RESEARCH

📆 ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

Image source: AI Futures Project

The Rundown: The AI Futures Project, the forecasting group behind AI 2027, just moved up its forecast for AI that matches the best human AI researchers up to 2027 — citing AI evaluator METR’s recent outside review of Anthropic’s AI speedup as its biggest reason.

The details:

  • The group’s paper published in 2025 depicted AI rapidly improving itself, but most of the authors later pushed their dates for AI that beats top experts into the 2030s.

  • METR estimated Anthropic now improves about 2x as fast, mostly thanks to AI, a pace the forecasters’ models gave under 4% odds of seeing this early.

  • Ex-OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo gave the earliest date, a 50-50 chance by May 2027, while the other five forecasters land between August and November.

  • Kokotajlo wrote on X that he is “scared, sad, and angry,” and the group says that if its forecast holds, a pause “should be the top priority for the AI industry.”

Why it matters: AI 2027 is considered one of the more prescient forecasts for how the industry has accelerated, and even its own authors said the pace shown in METR’s report caught them off guard. If their updated projections are as accurate as their old ones, the industry has months, not years, to prepare for the implications of superhuman AI research capabilities.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Polly built a caregiver recordkeeping app with Claude

Today’s workflow comes from reader Polly Bouker:

“My son is disabled and receives state funding for caregiving. The program requires daily records of what was done, whether he met his goals, and any behavioral or health issues. A program coordinator reviews these periodically, and an auditor may review them too. I used Claude to write the code for a web app built with Google tools that handles this recordkeeping.

Each day, caregivers open the app and check off each item on my son’s daily task list, which he completes with their help. The app writes the required daily summary from those check-offs and adds goal tracking. Everything goes into a printable report for the coordinator or an auditor.

My son has his own view showing how much of his list is checked off and how close he is to his favorite reward. Because he is motivated to see that he has earned the reward, he reminds the caregivers to complete their part.”
